title: Water-level changes at 22 large California reservoirs did not change the local share of small earthquakes in 1990-2025; the pooled effect is less than about 10% per 10 m
abstract: We tested if reservoir loads change local seismicity at 22 large California reservoirs (CDEC daily elevation, level ranges 15-73 m) in 1990-2025. We counted declustered USGS ComCat earthquakes of M 1.5 or more within 10 km of each reservoir and in a 20-40 km control ring. A conditional logistic model with reservoir effects related the near-zone share to the level anomaly, the monthly level change, lagged anomalies and the seasonal cycle. A permutation null shifted each level series by whole years. With 1,795 near-zone and 7,469 control events, the odds ratio was 0.991 per 10 m of level anomaly (bootstrap 95% interval 0.936-1.052, p = 0.85) and 0.872 per 10 m/month of level change (0.766-1.003, p = 0.17). Lags of 1-12 months and the seasonal cycle gave no effect. An any-sign test of per-reservoir slopes was null for all covariates. Injection tests give 80-86% power for an odds ratio of 1.10 or 1/1.10 per 10 m, so pooled effects of 10% or more per 10 m are unlikely; effects near 5% are not excluded. Eight sensitivity variants agreed. San Luis Reservoir showed a lower near-zone share in fast-filling months (p = 0.001), but this did not replicate in 1990-2007. A first run kept CDEC -9999 values and gave a false lag signal; corrected quality control removed it. Limitations: few events at most reservoirs, changing magnitude completeness, approximate shorelines, no Coulomb-stress or focal-mechanism model, and no first-filling cases. CDEC level series are not bundled; scripts regenerate them.
